note: Adapted from Hill (1927), Memoirs of the National Museum, Melbourne 7; the original combination is Microcerotermes taylori, n. sp. The measurement table is poorly preserved in the OCR and is not transcribed; the worker is described with 13- or 14-jointed antennae.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is related to M. nanus but differs in its darker colour, slightly larger eyes, 13-jointed antennae and distinctly different wing micrasters. The soldier differs from M. nanus in its shorter and narrower head, the sides less narrowed to the mandibles, longer and more slender mandibles, shorter and narrower labrum, and a gula about one-fourth narrower, markedly narrowed at the posterior third.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head shorter and narrower; mandibles longer and more slender; labrum shorter and narrower; gula about one-fourth narrower than in M. nanus and markedly narrowed at the posterior third; antennae 13-jointed.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head clay colour with very distinct pale sutures; postclypeus concolorous with the head, with a distinct brown median suture and a large dark chestnut spot at the internal mandibular articulation; antennae 13- or 14-jointed, the 3rd joint shortest, the 4th to the penultimate joint progressively longer, the apical joint markedly longer and a little narrower. It differs from M. nanus in the larger spots at the mandibular articulation, the dark median clypeal suture and the frons being concolorous with the back of the head rather than whitish.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Related to M. nanus; colour darker, eyes slightly larger, antennae 13-jointed, wing micrasters distinctly different. Head dark bay, postclypeus distinctly paler with a dark median suture; antennae 13-jointed, the 3rd joint shortest; eyes moderately large, ocelli broadly oval and very small; pronotum as in M. nanus.
